key_insight: The paper combines interpretable machine learning with data storytelling to make AI decisions understandable to non-experts while protecting sensitive data and model details.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical framework for explaining model outputs in real applications where transparency, usability, and privacy must be balanced.
method: Defines data storytelling in the context of IML using the DIST Pyramid and I-P-O Model.
Builds an explanation architecture that generates distinct "What-if" and "Why-not" narratives.
Uses data desensitization plus SHAP and LLMs to produce ABT-style stories.
evidence_signal: In a Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with significantly higher accessibility scores than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: The approach depends on LLM-generated narratives, so explanation fidelity, consistency, and privacy-preserving implementation need careful validation.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
